nodes.name: Mixing and evaporation
nodes.procedure: In a typical procedure, 0.018 mmol of ruthenium(III) chloride hydrate (RuCl₃·H₂O), 0.002 mmol of molybdenyl(VI) oxide bis(2,4-pentanedionate) [Mo(acac)₂], and 120 mg poly(vinyl pyrrolidone) were mixed in a glass bottle containing 10 ml of ethanol and stirred to obtain a clear solution. Then, the bottle was sealed and stirred at 60 rpm until the ethanol evaporated to obtain a gelatinous precursor.

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-MoRuO_x shows rutile RuO₂ crystal structure with broader diffraction peaks in (110) and (101) facets indicating amorphous-crystalline heterophase coexistence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns (Fig. 1B) showed that the MoRuO_x catalysts prepared at different annealing temperatures had the same rutile RuO₂ crystal structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-MoRuO_x displays abundant nanoareas from defects/porosity in amorphous regions with lattice spacing 0.334 nm assigned to RuO₂ (110) plane confirming AC coexistence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM image and enlarged image further revealed that defects or structural porosity were mainly distributed in amorphous regions ... lattice spacing (0.334 nm) of the crystal region was assigned to the (110) crystal plane of RuO₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Energy-dispersive x-ray mappings confirm homogeneous distribution of Ru, Mo, and O elements in AC-MoRuO_x.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding energy-dispersive x-ray element mappings (Fig. 1F) confirmed the homogeneous distribution of Ru, Mo, and O elements on AC-MoRuO_x.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3d peaks of AC-MoRuO_x slightly shifted with binding energies decreased by 0.3 eV compared to homemade RuO₂ and 0.4 eV compared to A-MoRuO_x, indicating reduced oxidation state of Ru sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From XPS results, the Ru 3d peaks of AC-MoRuO_x were slightly shifted, the binding energies decreased by 0.3 eV compared to the homemade RuO₂ and crystalline C-MoRuO_x, and the binding energy decreased by 0.4 eV compared to the amorphous A-MoRuO_x...

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-MoRuO_x has Brunauer-Emmett-Teller specific surface area of 153.8 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A Brunauer-Emmett-Teller specific surface area of 153.8 m²/g improves the accessibility of reactants to the catalytic sites...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge absorption position of AC-MoRuO_x located between Ru foil and Com RuO₂, lower than RuO₂ indicating lower Ru valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From Fig. 3A ... the Ru K-edge absorption position of AC-MoRuO_x was located between Ru foil and Com RuO₂ and lower than RuO₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-O bond length in AC-MoRuO_x stretched to 1.50 Å compared to 1.47 Å in Com RuO₂ due to lower Ru valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier-transformed extended x-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) (Fig. 3C) of the Ru K-edge suggested that the bond length of Ru-O in AC-MoRuO_x was slightly stretched to 1.50 Å compared with Com RuO₂ (1.47 Å).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS confirms elemental composition with Mo:Ru ratio lower than XPS-determined surface ratio, indicating Mo surface enrichment in AC-MoRuO_x.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably, the Mo:Ru ratio determined by XPS was consistently higher than that obtained from inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS), indicating the surface enrichment of Mo species...

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo K-edge absorption position of AC-MoRuO_x located between MoO₂ and MoO₃, closer to MoO₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Mo K-edge absorption position was located between MoO₂ and MoO₃ and closer to MoO₃ (Fig. 3B and fig. S39).
